commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot from Duke to Friday
Changed chatbot message to requirements
Add a echo feature and personality to chatbot for user inputs
Add the ability to display a list of items inputted by user
Add skill for codex to check its work
Bug fix where user can unmark work when it was not marked
Add deadline and to-do class
Add Events and integrate inheritance and polymorphism
Add exception handling and error testing
Allow user to delete task/event/to-do and error handling
Add validated task storage and round-trip regression tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce a Storage class to read and write UTF-8 records for todos,
deadlines, and events, preserving completion status and escaping special
characters so task text survives a save/load cycle.

Create missing parent folders, validate records before returning loaded
tasks, and write snapshots through a temporary file to avoid replacing
an existing save with an incomplete write. Add task-field getters so
persistence does not depend on console display strings.

Add dependency-free storage tests for missing files, round trips,
malformed records, large lists, and failed saves. All five test groups
pass with Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save Friday tasks automatically and verify restart behavior
commitResults.messageBody:
Load tasks at startup from the portable relative path data/friday.txt
and save after every addition, deletion, or completion-status change.
Replace the fixed task array with a list so larger saved lists load
without truncation or array-capacity failures.

Warn on read or write failures while keeping the console usable. Disable
saving after a failed load to protect existing data, and retry failed
writes on the next task-list change. Ignore local task data in Git and
document the storage format and recovery steps.

Run UI cases in isolated temporary directories and add restart, existing
save, special-character, corruption, and I/O-failure cases to the UI test
plan. All 23 UI cases pass with Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu. Additional live checks
confirm immediate saves, recovery after write failures, and persistence
after process termination.

commitResults.messageTitle: Record milestone commits and course-level publishing workflow
commitResults.messageBody:
Keep the user's standing preference to commit verified work at logical
milestones while leaving unrelated user edits out of those commits.

Document the explicit publishing procedure: merge each level branch
into master without fast-forwarding, tag the merge commit, and push
master, the retained level branch, and its tag to the fork. Continue
to require an explicit request before pushing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-7 into master to complete task persistence
commitResults.messageBody:
Bring in automatic saving and startup loading, validated task records,
protection for malformed or unreadable data, and isolated persistence
regression tests. Include the documented milestone commit workflow.

Use an explicit merge commit so the course checks can identify the
merged level branch and tag this completed milestone as Level-7.
The implementation passed 23 UI cases and five storage test groups
with Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu before merging.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add strict date-time parsing and readable date formatting
commitResults.messageBody:
Parse ISO dates, ISO dates with 24-hour times, and day-first dates with
HHmm times into LocalDateTime values. Treat date-only input as midnight
and accept the minute-precision ISO representation used by storage.

Use strict resolution so impossible dates and times are rejected, and
format dates with English month names regardless of the system locale.
Keep this behavior in a shared helper for consistent task handling.

Verify supported formats, leap days, malformed input, and display rules
with three passing date/time test groups on Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu.

commitResults.messageTitle: Store deadline and event dates as validated LocalDateTime values
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace free-form date fields with immutable LocalDateTime values and
format task dates using readable English month names. Reject invalid
calendar dates, invalid times, and events ending before they start
without adding tasks or terminating the command loop.

Persist minute-precision ISO date-times independently of the display
format. Continue to load older records with supported dates, and reject
ambiguous legacy date text without overwriting the original save file.
Document accepted formats, midnight behavior, and legacy-data recovery.

Update UI and storage fixtures to use real dates and add invalid-date,
leap-day, time-preservation, and legacy-file checks. All 28 UI cases,
four date/time test groups, and six storage test groups pass with
Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add date-based lookup for deadlines and events
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce on yyyy-MM-dd to find deadlines due on a date and events
whose inclusive calendar-date range contains it. Use polymorphic
occursOn methods so undated tasks are naturally excluded.

Keep original task numbers in filtered output so mark, unmark, and
delete still target the intended task. Include completed tasks, report
empty results, and reject invalid query dates without changing data.
Document inclusive event boundaries and the read-only query behavior.

All 31 UI cases, five date/time test groups, and six storage test groups
pass with Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu. A live-process check also confirms that
queries and rejected date inputs do not rewrite the save file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-8 into master to complete dates and times
commitResults.messageBody:
Bring in strict date/time parsing, LocalDateTime task fields, readable
date display, ISO persistence, and date-based deadline/event lookup.
Preserve invalid or ambiguous legacy saves instead of guessing dates.

Create an explicit merge commit for the Level-8 milestone and retain
the merged branch so the course checks can identify it. The branch
passed 31 UI cases, five date/time test groups, and six storage test
groups with Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu before merging.

commitResults.messageTitle: Require incremental level pushes and per-level README updates
commitResults.messageBody:
Record the standing workflow to develop each level in verified
increments, committing and pushing the level branch after each
meaningful milestone instead of waiting until the end of the level.

Require a root README summary for every level, relevant user-guide
updates, final verification, a no-fast-forward merge into master,
a lightweight level tag, and publication of both branches and the tag.

Add the missing Level 7 and Level 8 implementation summaries to the
README. Leave the user's unrelated ASCII-banner edit out of this commit.
Only documentation changes; validate the staged diff for whitespace.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract console interaction into a Ui class
commitResults.messageBody:
Move console input, separators, banners, task feedback, and storage
warnings out of Friday into Ui. Keep command parsing, task mutation,
and date filtering in Friday for this first OOP iteration so the
refactor changes one responsibility at a time.

Preserve existing command output, EOF handling, task numbering, and
save behavior. Reuse small presentation helpers for task details and
counts, and document the iteration and the planned TaskList extraction
in the README without including the unrelated banner edit.

Add a greeting/thanks regression case using output captured before the
refactor. All 32 UI cases, six storage test groups, and five date/time
test groups pass with Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract task collection operations into TaskList
commitResults.messageBody:
Move task membership, numbering, completion changes, and date filtering out
of Friday so the main loop coordinates Ui, TaskList, and Storage. Use
one-based task numbers consistently and report whether mark/unmark actually
changed a task, preserving the existing save-only-on-change behavior.

Copy the loaded collection and export an unmodifiable list copy for storage
to prevent outside structural changes. Reuse the existing task objects and
storage format rather than introduce a new persistence representation.

Add focused tests for numbering, deletion, completion changes, collection
ownership, and date queries. Extend the isolated UI helper to block a seeded
save after loading, and verify no-op status commands avoid unnecessary saves.
Document this iteration and the remaining Parser extraction in the README.
Console output and command behavior remain unchanged.

Verified with Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu:
- 33 command-driven UI cases
- 5 task-list test groups
- 6 storage test groups
- 5 date/time test groups

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract command parsing before reorganizing packages
commitResults.messageBody:
Preserve the existing Parser refactor as a separate prerequisite: centralize
command recognition and argument validation, delegate parsing from Friday,
and retain existing console errors and save behavior.

Include parser tests, the portable unit-test runner, and the corresponding
README and UI-plan updates so parsing can be verified independently before
moving classes into packages.

Verification: Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu; 21 unit-test groups and 34 UI cases pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Group task models and their tests in friday.task
commitResults.messageBody:
Move the six task-related classes into a cohesive domain package while
retaining src/main/java as the source root. Update callers and mirror task
tests under test/friday/task.

Make both test runners discover nested Java files and launch tests by their
qualified names so the reorganized sources remain covered. Document the
first package increment without changing commands or saved data.

Verification: Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu; 21 unit-test groups and 34 UI cases pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Separate application coordination from parsing storage and UI
commitResults.messageBody:
Move the entry point to friday.Friday and give Parser, Storage, and Ui their
own responsibility-based packages. Mirror parser/storage test packages and
update the UI runner, IntelliJ instructions, and command-line compilation
guidance so the packaged application remains easy to run.

Preserve all class bodies, console behavior, and the data/friday.txt format
and location. Keep src/main/java as the application source root.

Verification: Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu; 21 unit-test groups and 34 UI cases pass.
Package declarations match all 14 source/test paths; git diff --check passes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge codex/a-packages to complete A-Packages
commitResults.messageBody:
Integrate the existing UI and TaskList extractions, the separately verified
parser prerequisite, and the two package increments. Organize Friday by
responsibility while preserving src/main/java, console behavior, and saved
data. Include matching test packages, recursive test runners, and updated
launch documentation.

Retain a merge commit for the course workflow and keep codex/a-packages
available. Verified with Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu: 21 unit-test groups and 34 UI cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge Duke Gradle support and configure Friday build and run
commitResults.messageBody:
Integrate the upstream add-gradle-support branch while adapting its Gradle
9.6.1 wrapper to friday.Friday and Java 25. Preserve console standard input,
the project working directory, and src/main/java as the source root.
Pin the distribution SHA-256 and set a stable friday project name.

Keep this increment scoped to building and running: defer the upstream
JUnit and Shadow configuration to later course increments. Document Gradle
wrapper use, IntelliJ import, Java selection, troubleshooting, and the fact
that Gradle build does not yet run the existing main-method tests.

Verification with Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu: Gradle clean build succeeds; Gradle run
matches the greeting/thanks/bye UI case exactly; all 21 existing unit-test
groups and 34 UI cases pass. Wrapper JAR matches Gradle's official SHA-256.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge codex/a-gradle to complete A-Gradle
commitResults.messageBody:
Integrate the Duke add-gradle-support branch and the verified Friday-specific
build configuration. Use the checksum-pinned Gradle 9.6.1 wrapper with Java
25, preserve the source root and console input, and keep task data at the
project working directory. Include updated setup and troubleshooting docs.

Retain an explicit merge commit for the course workflow and keep the
feature branch. JUnit and Shadow configuration remain deferred to their
later increments; the existing regression runners remain unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit coverage for core task behavior and persistence
commitResults.messageBody:
Enable JUnit Jupiter 5.14.4 in Gradle using the platform BOM and explicit
launcher. Migrate the existing standalone regressions to src/test/java,
expand focused boundary and failure cases, and split task date behavior
into test classes matching the production classes. Keep the old Python
test entry point as a thin wrapper around the same Gradle test task.

Cover command parsing, one-based task operations and shallow snapshots,
strict date handling, inclusive event/deadline matching, and persistence
integrity including malformed input, escaping, partial writes and retries.
Use parameterized tests and isolated @TempDir fixtures without changing
production behavior or duplicating the old standalone Java suites.

Document the roughly 50% highest-value-method priority target in AGENTS.md
and CLAUDE.md and require relevant test updates after every code change.
Update setup and test documentation now that Gradle build runs JUnit.

Verification on Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu: 160 JUnit cases across six classes,
34 UI cases, clean build, exact Gradle console launch, and compatibility
runner pass. Isolated boundary and lenient-date mutations trigger test
failures and nonzero exit codes. Production sources remain unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge codex/a-junit to complete A-JUnit
commitResults.messageBody:
Integrate the verified JUnit migration and Gradle test configuration, keeping
src/main/java unchanged and placing six test classes under src/test/java.
Cover parsing, task operations, dates, and persistence with parameterized
cases and isolated file fixtures. Include the updated testing commands and
the AI documentation policy targeting the highest-value methods.

Preserve an explicit merge commit and retain the feature branch for the
course workflow. Verified on Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu: 160 JUnit cases, 34 UI cases,
Gradle clean build, console launch, and compatibility test runner.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document task APIs to meet the A-JavaDoc minimum
commitResults.messageBody:
Document all public methods and constructors in Task and TaskList, including parameters, return values, invalid task numbers, completion transitions, and shallow list snapshots.

Record the increment in README. Existing comments plus these additions cover all production classes and 32 of 54 public methods, meeting the minimum without changing application behavior.

Verified with Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu: all 160 JUnit tests pass and Gradle generates Javadoc successfully. Missing-documentation warnings remain outside this minimal increment; console output and saved data are unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-JavaDoc to complete minimal API documentation
commitResults.messageBody: Integrate the verified Task and TaskList documentation while preserving the independent CodingStandard and Level-9 branch starting points. This documentation-only increment meets the A-JavaDoc minimum without changing task behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Apply SE-EDU Java conventions
commitResults.messageBody:
Java sources mix switch indentation and comment styles, and some
boolean and collection names do not communicate their roles clearly.

Align production code and JUnit tests with the SE-EDU conventions.
Complete API headers while preserving console text, saved records,
and executable behavior.

Verify all 160 JUnit tests and 34 console cases with Java
25.0.3.fx-zulu. Confirm that executable tokens differ only by the
reviewed identifier renames.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add reusable Java and Git standard skills
commitResults.messageBody:
The project has no versioned guide for applying SE-EDU conventions
across coding sessions or reviewing future commit messages.

Add project skills with authoritative links, focused checklists, and
Friday-specific verification guidance. Record the coding-standard
increment in README so contributors can discover the skills.

Keep the skills in .agents/skills so they travel with the repository.
Validate both skill definitions with the skill-creator validator.

commitResults.messageTitle: Require project standards in AGENTS.md
commitResults.messageBody:
Agent guidance covers testing and Git workflow but does not require
reading the project's reusable Java and Git convention skills.

Require both skills for future Java work and commit messages,
including merge resolutions. Preserve existing scope, testing, and
Git authorization rules so style guidance does not expand access.

commitResults.messageTitle: Require project standards in CLAUDE.md
commitResults.messageBody:
Claude guidance delegates to AGENTS.md but does not name the project
skills that define Java and Git conventions.

Link both skills explicitly and require reading them for future
code changes, merge resolutions, and commit messages. Retain the
existing JUnit and console-testing guidance.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-CodingStandard into master
commitResults.messageBody:
The parallel documentation and coding-standard branches touch the
same task API comments and README insertion point.

Integrate the Java conventions and reusable project skills while
retaining the A-JavaDoc descriptions and both increment summaries.
Preserve the level branch for its independent implementation.

Resolve documentation punctuation conflicts without changing API
contracts, and retain both README summaries with a conflict reflection.
Verify all 160 JUnit tests and 34 console cases on the resolved
merge with Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu; Javadoc generation succeeds.
